summary: MPP mixes rails, so the rules follow the method. The card method, and the stripe method when the SPT carries a card, inherit card law, PSD2 strong customer authentication and network rules; an SPT can also carry other payment methods, such as Klarna and Affirm, which follow their own rules. Tempo and other stablecoin methods inherit stablecoin, anti-money-laundering, travel rule and sanctions rules. The core itself has no identity or screening layer beyond an optional payer identifier, and servers must not require user accounts for payment, so any screening falls to the sellers and settling parties that sanctions and AML rules reach. Rows give the date a fact was checked where it can change; check each source before relying on it.

rows.text: Tempo charges settle in TIP-20 stablecoins. The GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, 2025-07-18) regulates payment stablecoins and takes effect on the earlier of 2027-01-18 or 120 days after final regulations.

A Federal Register search on 2026-10-21 found no final rule implementing the GENIUS Act from a primary federal payment stablecoin regulator (OCC, FDIC, Federal Reserve, NCUA); their proposals include the OCC's, published 2026-03-02. Treasury's procedural interim final rule on state certifications took effect on 2026-09-30. Because no such final rule was issued by 2026-09-20, 120 days before 2027-01-18, the Act takes effect on 2027-01-18.
PYMNTS reported on 2026-08-19 that the Comptroller of the Currency said the OCC would have a final GENIUS Act rule out by November 2026.

The MPP core has no KYC or sanctions layer, and servers must not require user accounts for payment. OFAC says sanctions obligations are the same for digital and fiat currency transactions (FAQ 560): U.S. persons and others subject to OFAC jurisdiction must not deal with blocked persons, and OFAC says technology companies, users and payment processors should run risk-based programs that generally include sanctions list screening. With no screening in the protocol, that work falls to the sellers and settling parties within OFAC's reach.

FinCEN guidance FIN-2019-G001 (2019-05-09) judges intermediaries by four criteria, including whether they have total independent control over the value, and treats hosted wallet providers as money transmitters; a multiple-signature provider that only adds a validation key does not accept and transmit value. The guidance names no case of a seller's server that receives, broadcasts or fee-sponsors a payer-signed transfer, so how it applies to MPP servers is an inference.

Credit card charges through the stripe or card method fall under Regulation Z: unauthorized use means use without actual, implied or apparent authority, and cardholder liability is capped at the lesser of 50 USD or the amount obtained before notice. Debit and prepaid card charges fall under Regulation E instead. Whether an agent acting outside its instructions had apparent authority is untested.

Regulation E covers unauthorized electronic fund transfers from consumer accounts held by financial institutions; whether a transfer from a Tempo wallet counts is unclear. On 2026-10-21 Stripe's stablecoin payments docs listed no dispute support.

MiCA applies to e-money tokens and crypto-asset service providers; its transitional period for providers ended on 2026-07-01 at the latest (Member States could shorten or skip it), which matters for stablecoin methods offered to EU users.

The Transfer of Funds Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 has applied the travel rule since 2024-12-30 to crypto-asset transfers where the crypto-asset service provider of the originator or the beneficiary has its registered office in the Union, including transfers to or from self-hosted addresses. MPP chain credentials carry the payer's signed transfer (or the hash of one already broadcast) and the recipient's ledger address, and optionally a payer DID, but no names or other identifying data, so the rest of the travel-rule data must come from the providers involved.

Card charges inside the EU fall under PSD2 strong customer authentication and its RTS, including exemptions such as low-value remote payments up to EUR 30. In the stripe method, 3DS may be triggered when the client creates the SPT, after the 402 challenge and before it sends the credential.

AI Act transparency duties under Article 50 apply from 2026-08-02; generative systems placed on the market before that date have until 2026-12-02 for the Article 50(2) marking duty. The Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) moved Annex III high-risk obligations to 2027-12-02. Nothing in the AI Act is specific to agent payments.

GDPR covers information about an identifiable person, including online identifiers. Card credentials in the card method can carry billing address, cardholder name and payment account reference, which the card draft calls personally identifiable information, and public chain settlement exposes addresses that can be linked to a person.

The UK Money Laundering Regulations 2017 cover cryptoasset exchange providers and custodian wallet providers carrying on business in the UK (regulations 8 and 14A), and Part 7A has applied the travel rule to their cryptoasset transfers since 2023-09-01. An MPP stablecoin payment is in scope only when such a business sends or receives it, including transfers between it and an unhosted wallet.
The UK Payment Services Regulations 2017 tie liability to consent (regulation 67) and limit payer liability for unauthorized transactions (regulation 77), which applies to card-based MPP charges.
The FCA payments priorities (2026-03-25) include agentic AI, and HM Treasury consulted on modernising payment services regulation from 2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06.

Canada's Stablecoin Act in Bill C-15 received Royal Assent on 2026-03-26 but is not yet in force (Justice Laws, current to 2026-09-30); Finance Canada expects the framework to come into force in 2027.

The Retail Payment Activities Act's risk management and funds safeguarding requirements have applied since 2025-09-08, after registration opened on 2024-11-01, bringing payment service providers under Bank of Canada supervision; its assessment-fee provisions (Part 6) are not yet in force.

A business providing digital payment token services in Singapore needs a MAS license under the Payment Services Act 2019 unless exempt. MAS finalized a framework on 2023-08-15 for single-currency stablecoins pegged to the Singapore dollar or a G10 currency and issued in Singapore, and on 2026-09-01 consulted on amending the Act to implement it; stablecoins outside it, such as those issued abroad, remain digital payment tokens.
MAS issued Guidelines on AI Risk Management for financial institutions on 2026-10-07, effective 2027-10-07, and plans to consult on agentic AI guidance in 2027.

Card routes keep card network rules: the card method carries an encrypted network token that the server's Server Enabler decrypts and submits to the card network for authorization, and reversibility follows network chargeback rules. As of 2026-10-21 no MPP-specific card pricing or liability rule was found. Stripe's US pricing page lists Shared Payment Tokens, which the stripe method carries, at 0.15 USD per SPT issued without naming the party billed.

Visa's rules govern Visa and its member institutions and yield to applicable law. Since 2025-10-18 they have required an Agentic Payment Provider to enroll in Visa Intelligent Commerce and register with Visa, directly or via an Agentic Payment Enabler. Within Visa's system, they make the cardholder responsible for the provider's actions in an Agentic Transaction as if the cardholder had initiated it, and for disputes processed from 2026-10-24 they accept the provider's login ID among the evidence that can defeat a card-absent fraud dispute. The card method's draft recommends agent-specific tokens from services such as Visa Intelligent Commerce.

The stripe method keeps raw payment method details away from the client, which its spec says reduces PCI DSS scope. The card method encrypts the network token so that neither client nor server can read it; the card draft says nothing about PCI DSS.
